co_live_action_wall.blurb: A quiet bolted wall high on the north flank of Clear Creek Canyon, west of Golden, tucked between the Creek Side and Safari crags. All 24 climbs here are sport routes, mostly one pitch, ranging from roughly 5.8 up to the low 5.12s. The bulk of the lines sit in the 5.10 to 5.11 band, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on steep, sustained face climbing rather than first-timers. The rock matches the canyon's gneiss. The wall faces south and soaks up sun, which makes it pleasant in cooler months and warm in summer. It sees far fewer visitors than the canyon's roadside walls, and the walk in is a steady uphill hike of about twenty minutes.

co_december_wall.blurb: A broad granite band west of Lyons, high above the highway on the north wall of the canyon cut by the South Fork of St. Vrain Creek. The 24 climbs here are mostly traditional lines on cracks and corners, with a handful of sport routes and one aid line. Grades cluster around 5.9 to 5.11, with a few easier pitches and one harder test piece. Many routes are multi-pitch. The cliff splits into a longer left side of older crack routes and a small steep alcove on the right. Quality is uneven and some sections are loose, so expect to pick your lines. Facing south, it warms quickly and stays climbable through much of the year; summer afternoons can be hot.

co_jackson_creek_dome.blurb: A granite dome of roughly 300 feet in the Rampart Range, south of Sedalia and part of the Jackson Creek cluster of crags. It is known for friction on clean slabs: the south face carries bolted slab lines, many of them two pitches, while the southeast side mixes cracks with slabs. Most of the 24 climbs here are sport, with a few trad lines and top-rope options, and grades fall mostly between 5.8 and 5.10 with a smaller number of 5.11s. Some bolted routes have long runouts on easier ground, so small cams are a useful supplement. A remote, forested setting with a short uphill walk to reach the rock.

co_quarry_the.blurb: A granite crag in the South Platte country of the Front Range, part of the Thunder Ridge complex and among the first formations reached on the walk in past the burn zone and aspens. The main wall faces south, with a west-facing wall beside it and an east-facing one nearby, so there is usually somewhere to find sun or shade. Of the 24 climbs, most are trad with a handful of bolted routes and a single boulder problem. Grades are centred on 5.9 to 5.11, with a few easier lines and some 5.12 testpieces at the top end. The surrounding ridge is remote and lightly visited, so crowds are rarely an issue.

co_snake_eyes_wall.blurb: A compact sport wall in the Narrows stretch of Poudre Canyon, west of Fort Collins, close to the Eden area. It walls in a steep gully on the left and looks east, with a bright orange band of pegmatite running up the face. Of the 24 climbs, most are single-pitch bolted lines, with a few trad and top-rope routes, mostly 40 to 85 feet long. Grades run from easy to 5.12, but the weight sits in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so it suits stronger sport climbers. Quality is mixed, with a few popular standouts alongside lesser lines. The gully below is loose and prickly with burrs.
